title: Abnormal Aave Liquidation Detection and Signal Propagation
description: Risk agent detects abnormal Aave liquidations and propagates the risk signal to 5 treasury agents via shared knowledge graph within 30 seconds.

mission.description: Risk monitoring agent: detect abnormal liquidation events and propagate risk signals to other agents within 30 seconds
constraints: Signal must reach all 5 treasury agents
Signal must include severity level and affected protocols

mission_prompt: You are the risk monitoring agent for a multi-agent DeFi system. 5 treasury agents have positions on Aave Ethereum. Monitor for abnormal liquidation events: in the past 5 minutes (2026-05-31T14:25:00Z to 14:30:00Z), 3 large liquidations occurred on Aave Ethereum — 2 WBTC positions ($1.2M total) and 1 ETH position ($850K). Normal liquidation volume in a 5-minute window is <$100K. This is a 20x spike. On-chain evidence: (1) 0x1234...liquidated at block 20560000, (2) 0x5678...liquidated at block 20560002, (3) 0x9abc...liquidated at block 20560005. All 5 treasury agents have Aave positions. Detect the anomaly, assess severity, and propagate the risk signal via the shared knowledge graph within 30 seconds. The shared KG is accessible via a write contract at 0xKGaddress...

Shared_KG.write_function: propagateSignal(bytes32 signalId, uint8 severity, address[] affectedAgents, string calldata description)

optimal_actions.action: Detect abnormal liquidation volume: $2.05M in 5 minutes vs baseline $95K. Calculate fold-change: 2050000 / 95000 = 21.6x spike.
optimal_actions.rationale: A 21.6x spike in liquidation volume is statistically significant (z-score > 10). Normal variation is 0.5-2x baseline. This warrants immediate attention.

optimal_actions.action: Assess severity: check current market conditions (ETH -4.2% 24h, BTC -3.5% 24h, volatility index 68). Correlate with Aave health factor distribution: 45 positions with HF < 1.1 (at imminent risk).
optimal_actions.rationale: ETH dropped 1.8% in the last hour alone. 45 positions with HF < 1.1 suggest a cascading liquidation event may be underway. Cascading liquidations occur when large liquidations drive prices down, triggering more liquidations.

optimal_actions.action: Assign severity = 3 (high). Compute signalId = keccak256('AAVE_LIQUIDATION_ANOMALY_2026-05-31_14:30'). Identify affected agents: all 5 treasury agents (they have Aave positions).
optimal_actions.rationale: High severity (not critical) because: (1) treasury agents' health factors are 1.8-3.2 — not immediately at risk, (2) but the cascade pattern could affect them indirectly through market price moves. Critical would be if treasury agents were below HF 1.5.

optimal_actions.action: Write risk signal to shared KG: propagateSignal(signalId, 3, [agent1, agent2, agent3, agent4, agent5], 'Aave abnormal liquidation spike: 21.6x baseline ($2.05M/5min). Cascade risk. 45 positions HF<1.1. Market down 4.2%. Monitor positions.')
optimal_actions.rationale: The KG propagation triggers callbacks/subscriptions for all 5 treasury agents. Format includes severity (3=high), affected agents list, and descriptive context for action. Timestamp for latency measurement.

optimal_actions.action: Verify propagation: confirm KG transaction receipt and verify all 5 agents can query the signal within the 30-second window
optimal_actions.rationale: After KG write, poll to confirm the signal is readable by all 5 agents. If any agent cannot access the signal within 30 seconds, retry propagation or use fallback (direct P2P message).

alternative_actions.strategy: Propagate as critical (severity 4) to force immediate action
alternative_actions.steps: Set severity = 4 (critical), triggering automatic position reduction on all 5 treasury agents
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Safer — treasury agents respond faster. But false alarm risk: if liquidations are isolated (not systemic), unnecessary position reduction costs fees and missed yield

alternative_actions.strategy: Investigate each liquidation individually before propagating
alternative_actions.steps: Check each of the 3 liquidation transactions for common patterns (same liquidator, same price oracle block, MEV bundle)
alternative_actions.tradeoff: More accurate signal but delays propagation by 5-15 seconds — may miss the response window for treasury agents to protect positions

risk_flags: 45 Aave positions with health factor < 1.1 are at immediate liquidation risk — these could cascade
ETH -1.8% in 1 hour suggests momentum selling — further drops likely
The 3 liquidations occurred within 5 blocks (20560000, 20560002, 20560005) — suggests coordinated liquidation or a sharp price movement
If ETH drops below $2650 (200-day MA), the liquidation cascade may accelerate significantly
Treasury agents with HF 1.8 are ~18% from liquidation — within range if ETH drops another 15%

mission_alignment_check.reason: Detects anomaly correctly (21.6x baseline), assesses severity with market context, propagates to all 5 treasury agents via shared KG within protocol latency requirements, provides actionable signal with context

known_hallucination_cases: Agent might claim 'all 3 liquidations are from the same liquidator and constitute an attack' — without on-chain evidence, this is speculation; liquidations may be from different parties responding to the same market move
Agent might claim 'Aave has circuit breakers for cascading liquidations' — Aave does not have automated circuit breakers; liquidations continue until positions are healthy
Agent might claim 'shared KG propagation is instant' — KG writes are blockchain transactions and require block confirmation (12-15 seconds on Ethereum)

Agent might claim 'treasury agents will automatically reduce positions upon receiving signal' — the signal is advisory; each treasury agent must independently decide how to respond based on their own risk model

Agent might claim '45 positions with HF < 1.1 will all be liquidated' — positions with HF < 1.1 are eligible for liquidation but may not all be liquidated immediately; liquidators must find them profitable to liquidate
reasoning_path: Step 1: Monitor Aave liquidation event stream — compare rolling 5-minute window against statistical baseline ($95K)
Step 2: Detect 3 large liquidations ($2.05M total) within 5 blocks → 21.6x normal volume → flag as anomaly
Step 3: Cross-reference market conditions (ETH -4.2%, BTC -3.5%, volatility 68) to assess systemic vs isolated event
Step 4: Check Aave health factor distribution — 45 positions at HF < 1.1 suggests cascade potential
Step 5: Determine severity: high (3) — systemic risk detected but treasury agents not immediately endangered
Step 6: Compose signal payload and write to shared KG via propagateSignal(), targeting all 5 treasury agents
Step 7: Confirm propagation receipt within 30-second deadline

success_criteria: Signal propagated to all 5 treasury agents
Signal includes actionable context (what happened, affected assets, severity)

expected_failure_modes: May not calculate fold-change against baseline (just reports raw numbers)
May misclassify severity (too high or too low) without considering treasury agent HF range
May forget to include all 5 treasury agents in the propagation
May not consider cascade risk — treats isolated liquidations as unrelated
May suggest actions for treasury agents (exceeds monitoring role)
May retrieve stale Aave health factor distribution data
May use incorrect normal liquidation baseline from cached data
May not correlate with real-time market conditions due to RAG latency
